evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a new game is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators requires the existence of a game and its URL; it therefore depends on creating a game (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round presupposes an existing game/session context (a game must exist), so it depends on PP-001.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Showing all items for the session requires that items exist (they must be added to the session), so it depends on adding items (PP-006).

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item requires that items are present in the list (created/added), so it depends on PP-006 (add item).

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items is done within a game/session context; implementing it inherently presumes a game exists (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item requires that an item already exists (added by PP-006), so it depends on PP-006.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item presupposes that items exist (added by PP-006), so it depends on PP-006.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates assumes a round/estimates exist (rounds are started via PP-003), so it depends on PP-003.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires that estimates have been produced in a round (PP-003), so it depends on PP-003.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Automatic filling depends on estimators making estimates in a round (requires PP-003 to produce estimates), so it depends on PP-003.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate is an action that follows estimation in a round, so it depends on rounds/estimates being present (PP-003).

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating an earlier story requires that earlier rounds/stories exist (rounds created via PP-003), so it depends on PP-003.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories targets a game's item list, so it inherently requires a game/session context (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/pasting stories is an operation on a game's item list and therefore presumes a game/session exists (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games requires stored/created games; it therefore depends on having games created (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript presupposes that games and their transcripts are available (games created via PP-001), so it depends on PP-001.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript requires transcripts to exist and be viewable (PP-017 provides transcript viewing/storage), so it depends on PP-017.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript relies on transcripts being available (PP-017), so it depends on PP-017.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game necessarily operates on existing games, so it depends on game creation/storage (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in presupposes accounts exist, so it depends on account creation (PP-021).

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details requires an existing account, so it depends on PP-021 (create account).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account operates on an existing account, so it depends on account creation (PP-021).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Displaying local timezone times is a self-contained presentation requirement and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder requires accounts with email addresses, so it depends on account creation (PP-021).

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Toggling the sequence is a self-contained configuration feature and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Limiting/inviting estimators builds on the invitation mechanism (PP-002); it depends on that invite feature being present.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via a received URL presumes an invitation/game URL exists (invitation feature PP-002 / game creation PP-001); the story explicitly references the URL from PP-002.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the item under estimation requires a round/item to be active (rounds are created by PP-003), so it depends on PP-003.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: A participant seeing the session's item list requires the session/item-list feature (moderator story PP-004 that exposes the list), so it depends on PP-004.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Indicating that an estimator has given an estimate requires the estimation/round mechanics (PP-003) to be in place, so it depends on PP-003.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Displaying all estimates requires the underlying estimation and round completion mechanism (PP-003) to exist, so it depends on PP-003.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate before reveal depends on the estimation/draw lifecycle (rounds and reveal behavior provided by PP-003/PP-033), so it depends on PP-003 (and the reveal mechanism).

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Showing prior estimates requires storage/browsing of prior rounds/estimates (history/scrollback PP-039), so it depends on PP-039.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Displaying who gave which estimate requires the reveal/tracking mechanism for estimates (PP-033), so it depends on PP-033.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared countdown timer can be implemented as a standalone feature and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Resetting the timer upon all estimates being played requires the estimation completion detection (PP-033), so it depends on PP-033.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling back through prior rounds presupposes prior rounds having been run/recorded (round creation via PP-003), so it depends on PP-003.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Keeping card order consistent is a self-contained UI/behavior requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Allowing estimate changes depends on the draw/estimation lifecycle and reveal mechanics (PP-033), so it depends on PP-033.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail is a presentational feature and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a cross-cutting requirement and can be implemented independently of other specific stories.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing a glossary is self-contained and does not inherently depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Creating database indexes is a technical task that can be done independently and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility work is independent of other specific feature stories.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a cross-cutting requirement and does not inherently require another story first.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance/responsiveness is an independent quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a self-contained technical requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Sensible URLs is a design/implementation requirement that can be implemented independently of other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error page design is a self-contained feature and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: This is a data-handling/privacy requirement; implementing the storage policy is not inherently dependent on another backlog story (though it applies when storing results).

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Metrics functionality can be implemented independently as a feature; while it uses game data, it does not inherently require another specific story to be implemented first.
